findings.summary: The stage order is written as a flat list of eight names, so a learner cannot see it as a sequence or see which stages are cheap and fast.
findings.evidence: "Checkout Install Lint Test Build Package Staging Production"
findings.fix: Draw it as a left-to-right flow with arrows, and mark the cheap fast checks (Lint, Test) as run first.

findings.summary: The `needs:` rule is shown only as prose, and the stage-order page never ties the `needs:` fan-in to its YAML.
findings.evidence: "needs: orders jobs; without it jobs run in parallel" followed by `needs: [test, deploy-staging]`
findings.fix: Add a small diagram of test and deploy-staging feeding into deploy-prod, with an approval gate before it.

findings.summary: The section does not cover an outline point (missing "operating", "strategy").
findings.evidence: Pass config with env:, secrets.NAME and the matrix: strategy for running across versions or operating systems
findings.fix: Add the point with an explanation and an example.

findings.summary: The minimal workflow YAML leaves out the `on:` trigger, so the page's example is not a complete workflow and relies on a separate prose line to finish it.
findings.evidence: "Add on: [push] above jobs:" and the yaml block that starts at "jobs:"
findings.fix: Put `on: [push]` as the first line of the yaml block and delete the "Add on: [push] above jobs:" line.

findings.summary: One bullet holds two ideas, parallel execution and runner assignment.
findings.evidence: "Jobs run in parallel, each on its own runner (runs-on: ubuntu-latest)"
findings.fix: Split it into "Jobs run in parallel" and "Each job gets its own runner: runs-on: ubuntu-latest".
